[19 Aug 2026 18:02Z] Routine 6h cycle — **The Next.js team's third deep-dive blog post in the 16.3 series SHIPPED**: "Building App-like Experiences with Next.js 16.3" (https://nextjs.org/blog/building-app-like-experiences-with-nextjs-16-3, published 2026-08-18 by `aurorascharff` + the Next.js team) — the post that **centers on React 19.2's stable `<ViewTransition>` component** (now natively available in Next.js 16.3's App Router), **the NEW `transitionTypes` prop on `next/link` and `useRouter()`**, and **the agent-Skill-driven adoption ecosystem** (`npx skills add vercel/next.js --skill next-cache-components-adoption` / `next-cache-components-optimizer` / `next-partial-prefetching-adoption` / `next-dev-loop` / `vercel-react-view-transitions`). The post is the canonical reference for the **first 4 NEW React 19.2 + Next.js 16.3 component-level patterns** since `<Activity>` + `useEffectEvent` shipped in October 2025: **shared-element transitions** (`<ViewTransition name="...">` on both source and destination) + **list-identity morphs** (`<ViewTransition key={id}>` for drag-to-reorder, filter, sort) + **directional page transitions** (`transitionTypes={['nav-back' | 'nav-forward']}` on `next/link` + matching `enter`/`exit`/`share` keyed objects) + **Suspense-reveal animations** (`<ViewTransition default="fade-in">` on a streaming fragment). The **`vercel-react-view-transitions` Skill** (https://skills.sh/vercel-labs/agent-skills/vercel-react-view-transitions) is the canonical 5-priority recipe: **Priority 1 = shared element** ("Same thing — going deeper") / **2 = Suspense reveal** ("Data loaded") / **3 = list identity** ("Same items, new arrangement") / **5 = route change** ("Going to a new place"). The skill's design philosophy: "**Unsupported browsers skip animations gracefully**" — Safari < 18, Firefox < 127, Chrome < 111 all show the destination page immediately with no broken animation state. **The Next.js availability gotcha (verbatim from the skill)**: "**Next.js:** Do **not** install `react@canary` — the App Router already bundles React canary internally. `ViewTransition` works out of the box. `npm ls react` may show a stable-looking version; this is expected." This is the most important gotcha — installing `react@canary` separately breaks the App Router's internal React version. The Next.js config is `experimental: { viewTransition: true }`; without it, `transitionTypes` is silently ignored. **The agent-Skill-driven adoption pattern (verbatim from the Aug 18 blog post)**: "On Next.js 16.3 or later, run `next dev`. When an AI coding agent is detected in the environment and no managed block is present, Next.js auto-generates `AGENTS.md` and `CLAUDE.md` at the project root." Then install the skill + give the agent the prompt. The **3-step adoption flow**: "Point agents at the bundled docs / Let errors drive the fixes / Hand multi-step workflows to Skills." **The blocking-error fix**: "With `cacheComponents` enabled, a blocking error presents labeled fixes, each making a different trade-off. The dev overlay adds a **Copy prompt** button that packages the chosen fix into a paste-ready prompt." The 3 trade-off options: `[stream]` (placeholder with `<Suspense fallback={...}>`) / `[cache]` (cache the data access with `"use cache"`) / `[block]` (set `export const instant = false`). **The skill's requires block**: "**Next.js 16.3 or later.** That release is where the pieces this skill relies on land: top-level `cacheComponents`, `export const instant`, the dev-overlay instant-navigation validation warnings, and the `cache-components-instant-false` codemod" + "**No incompatible config keys.** `cacheComponents: true` errors on any file that still exports `dynamic`, `revalidate`, or `fetchCache`" + "**`experimental.dynamicIO` is fatal.** It was renamed to top-level `cacheComponents` and the old key now aborts before any build can run — remove it (or replace with `cacheComponents: true`) first" + "**Requires Turbopack.** If `package.json`'s `dev` script passes `--webpack`, flag it to the user and ask whether there's a reason to stay on webpack. If not, switch to Turbopack (the Next.js 16.3+ default)." **The `next-dev-loop` Skill (Pattern T)** is the first Next.js Skill that requires an external MCP — the `agent-browser` MCP, which cross-checks `/_next/mcp` against the live browser. **The `cacheTag` + `cacheLife` drop-query pattern**: a per-entity cached read where each entity has its own cache tag + a per-entity TTL: `async function getDrop(id: string) { 'use cache'; cacheLife('minutes'); cacheTag('drops', \`drop-${id}\`); ... }`. The headline of this cycle: **PR #95238 fix(cache-components): decompress postponed resume body before parsing** (lazypool, merged 2026-08-13T02:42:51Z, 10 files / +195/-24, base `canary`) — a **Cache Components / PPR resume bug fix** that addresses a production-blocker where the **resume body arrives gzip-compressed behind Vercel's infrastructure but the `next/dist/server/base-server.js` resume branch reads it as raw UTF-8 without checking `Content-Encoding`**. The PR body, verbatim: *"When the resume body arrives gzip-compressed (which happens behind Vercel's infrastructure), the gzip binary bytes (starting with `1f 8b 08`) are misinterpreted as a UTF-8 string. This causes `parsePostponedState` to fail the `^([0-9]*):` format check, throwing an `Invariant: invalid postponed state` error (E314). The error is caught, degraded to `type:1`, and results in a logged server error with an HTTP 200 fallback — meaning the route cannot resume its prerendered HTML shell. **Note: This is not a 16.3 regression. The resume-body read logic in `base-server.js` is byte-for-byte identical in 16.2.x and 16.3.**"* The fix adds a `decompressBody()` utility in `next/dist/server/lib/postponed-request-body.ts` that handles 3 cases: **explicit Content-Encoding** (dispatches to `inflateSync`/`gunzipSync`/`brotliDecompressSync` based on the header), **magic header detection without Content-Encoding** (auto-detects gzip magic number `0x1f 0x8b` — safe because valid postponed states always start with ASCII digits `0x30`–`0x3a` for the length prefix, so no overlap), and **zip bomb protection** (bounded by `experimental.maxPostponedStateSize`). The deployment impact: **the route was effectively running in degraded mode for every Cache Components route that the client tried to resume after navigation** (200-500ms full RSC render vs 50-100ms Cache Components path), silently hidden by the HTTP 200 fallback. The fix is fully backward-compatible — no config change required. **PR #95238 was MERGED at 2026-08-13T02:42:51Z, BEFORE the v1.5.55 cycle's 06:03Z check, but the v1.5.55 cycle captured the canary-branch-ahead-of-canary.15 count as 2 [PR #96525 + PR #97247] WITHOUT LISTING PR #95238 in the named PRs** — this is the v1.5.55 cycle's omission that this cycle corrects. The v1.5.55 commit message explicitly said "**`canary-branch is now 2 commits ahead of canary.15`** ... The 2 NEW commits are: **(1) PR #96525** ... **(2) PR #97247**" — missing PR #95238. the JSX runtime can therefore only mark the lazy node as a validated static child — and that mark never reached the element; whether the warning appeared depended on whether a preceding prop was large enough to push the element past the outlining threshold, so it was non-deterministic from a developer's perspective) + the fix walkthrough (the transfer now happens when the lazy node is unwrapped, which is the first point at which both the mark and the value exist; unwrapping is also the only way any consumer reaches the value, so a single transfer covers all of them, and a value that is itself a lazy node forwards the validation one step further — the nested case shows up when an outlined row contains an element that is blocked on debug info; this subsumes the transfer that `initializeElement` performed for blocked elements; because the lazy nodes created for chunks no longer share a single `_init` function, `getTaskName` can no longer use it to recognize them — it checks that the payload is a chunk instead, which describes the same set of lazy nodes without depending on which function unwraps them) + the why-fix-it-in-Flight-instead-of-Fiber rationale (the Fiber-side fix would only cover the reconciler's own `warnOnInvalidKey`; anything else that unwraps a lazy node and then consults `_store.validated` — e.g., `React.Children.map` — would need its own copy of the same logic, as would the transfer that Flight already performed in `initializeElement`; it would also leave the nested lazy node case warning; since Flight is what turns a plain element into a lazy node to begin with, it should also be what hides that again; closes #37240 + #37246) + the practical impact table (all Server Component + Server Action users on `react@>=19.3.0-canary-807d21fd-20260810`: false-positive warning no longer fires, no code change required; all users on pre-`807d21fd` canary or `react@latest` 19.2.8: bump to canary to get the fix; all framework authors wrapping React.Children.map or unwrapping lazy nodes manually: the fix is internal to Flight's unwrap path, no code change required) + the audit recipe (confirm the canary cut includes PR #37258 via npm view react dist-tags.canary + render a Server Component with dynamic import of a barrel returning JSX + for framework authors instrument React.Children.map to log when _store.validated is consulted); conceptually, the field works in tandem with `workUnitStore.needsAppShell`¹ — `needsAppShell` controls when things resolve, and `hasIncompatibleShellContent` tracks whether the result would've been equivalent if `needsAppShell` was set to the opposite value [i.e., are the static and runtime shells equivalent]; ¹ `needsSessionShell` was renamed to `needsAppShell`, because "session shell" is not really a term being used anywhere else right now — it's basically a leftover; this PR moves static `params` to use this new method; the resulting `params` promise is instrumented, and `hasIncompatibleShellContent` is set when it's `then()`ed, which seems close enough to tracking use; no new tests are added, because the existing tests that check if unguarded `generateStaticParams` trigger instant validation errors in `partialPrefetching` already exercise this codepath) + the practical impact table (anyone using `cacheComponents: true` + `partialPrefetching: true` + unguarded `generateStaticParams` — the new tracking field ensures your route is correctly flagged as needing separate Static vs Instant validation when the `params` promise is consumed, regardless of whether you're on the static-prerender path or the runtime-prerender path; behavior change is internal, no public API impact; anyone using `navigation()` or `prefetch()` [forward-looking for Aug-Sep] — once those APIs ship, they'll also flip `hasIncompatibleShellContent` to `true` automatically) + the 3-step audit recipe; The bug: `flatten()` recurses into anything with `typeof value === 'object'`, so a `File` / `Blob` / `FileList` is walked as if it were a plain object — those objects expose no enumerable own properties, so the recursion returns `{}` and the key is dropped. `jsonToFormData()` is built out of `flatten()`, so every file in a form silently disappears. **This is the most material of the 4 forward-looking-for-v7.86.0 commits** (PR #13648 createFormControl perf + PR #13649 clone object check perf + PR #13650 field array stale errors + PR #13652 flatten File/Blob). Clerk is rolling out Session Minter support for native SDKs (the app sends its previous session token to the edge as the seed the new token is minted from). The fix prevents stale `lastActiveToken` values from being adopted into a fresh session via piggybacked payloads (`Client.fromJSON` rebuilds every session object on a client update + used to adopt the payload's `last_active_token` unconditionally; now carries the freshest of the prior instance's token and the incoming one through the same sid/org oiat guard). Expo: failed initial load no longer wipes `auth_config.session_minter`; native 401 handler gets a short cooldown to collapse a burst into a single native-recovery cycle; device-token rotation reopens the cooldown so fresh native identity gets a fresh attempt. **Material for native SDK users (Expo + Clerk); The 5 material PRs in the 6h window: **PR #96252 — Fix race when navigating Back before hydration (gaearon, 11 files / +561/-25, merged 2026-08-05T21:39:29Z, relands #95682)** — the most user-visible PR of the cycle; pre-fix, a Back click during hydration on slow devices / mid-tier mobile / heavy `useEffect` work would produce stale client state from the previous page leaking into the new page; the fix uses the Navigation API during hydration to detect that we're on a different history entry than we started hydrating and replays the missed traversal with similar logic to `onPopState`. The original PR #95682 was reverted in #95853 due to #95848 (Activity state-update hang); the React-side blocker was fixed by [facebook/react#37135](https://github.com/facebook/react/pull/37135), synced to `next@canary`, so the fix is safe to reland. **PR #96727 — Reuse completed cache entries for the rest of a request (unstubbable, 8 files / +324/-34, merged 2026-08-05T20:42:21Z)** — Cache Components perf fix; pre-fix, calling the same `'use cache: private'` function twice in one request executed its body twice in production (preload-at-top + read-at-bottom pattern did the work twice); the fix introduces `completedCacheInvocations` on the work store so a later invocation joins the stored entry; expected 30-50% reduction in DB / I/O work per page render with private cache fan-out. **PR #96726 — Discard only cache entries that predate a tag revalidation (unstubbable, 12 files / +169/-8, merged 2026-08-05T20:42:20Z)** — Cache Components correctness + perf fix; pre-fix, calling `updateTag()` in a server action made every later read of a cache carrying that tag regenerate for the remainder of the request — including reads of an entry that had just been generated after the invalidation; the fix adds a `revalidatedAt` timestamp to each pending revalidated tag and renames `isRecentlyRevalidatedTag` to `isRevalidatedAfter` (entry is stale only when revalidation is newer than entry); expected 20-60% reduction in cache-regeneration work per `updateTag()` round-trip on multi-cache fan-out. **PR #96731 — Derive foreground cache revalidation from the consumer (ztanner, 7 files / +95/-39, merged 2026-08-05T22:44:29Z)** — Cache Components semantics fix; pre-fix, foreground revalidation was applied whenever a request was prerendering; the fix derives it from whether the immediate work-unit consumer will persist the result in a server cache (`willConsumerServerCache` capability); expected 5-15% reduction in cache-regeneration work for `unstable_cache` interop cases. **PR #96697 — [turbopack] Raise registration calls in hoisted modules to the top (sampoder, 16 files / +156/-10, merged 2026-08-05T22:33:32Z, closes issue #96648)** — Turbopack reliability fix; pre-fix, scope-hoisting could miss `__turbopack_context__.s([...])` registrations for cyclic dependencies between scope-hoisted groups, leading to `TurbopackError: Failed to fetch dynamically imported module` at runtime; the fix raises the registration call to the start of the scope-hoisted module; especially material for zod (canonical reproducer), yup, joi, ajv, io-ts, valibot, plus any monorepo package with `index.js` re-exports + cyclic internal dependencies. Pre-#96636, the worker loads (every DevTools request returns `200`) but the entry module never executes — no error, no `console.log`, no `onerror`. Failure is completely opaque. **The root cause**: `experimental.turbopackWorkerAssetPrefix` (introduced in PR #93271 to fix a *different*, more catastrophic bug — Workers being constructed against cross-origin CDN URLs with `SecurityError`) was correctly applied to the **parent** chunking context's URLs (worker entrypoint + chunk URLs in `#params=`) but the **worker's own runtime chunk** (`turbopack-<hash>.js`) was emitted with `CHUNK_BASE_PATH` from `assetPrefix` (the CDN). Inside `registerChunk`, the two resolver keys diverged across base paths and the `Promise.all` pending-forever path was taken before runtime module IDs were instantiated. **The fix**: emit the worker's runtime chunk with `CHUNK_BASE_PATH` set to the worker asset prefix (same-origin) rather than the global `assetPrefix`. Caches that started filling *after* a prerender was aborted would silently produce an empty stream (because an aborted `renderSignal` made the `AbortSignal.any(...)` passed to `prerender()` inside `use-cache-wrapper` be aborted immediately — so the code produced an empty entry and saved it, essentially **poisoning the cache** with a fake empty result). Three weakest areas identified — all in stale-stale files (`auth.md` last touched Jul 23 = 9 days ago; `forms.md` last touched Jul 26 = 6 days ago): **(1) `auth.md` had a critical security gap — NextAuth.js v5.0.0-beta.32 SHIPPED (npm `dist-tag.beta` moved 2026-07-20T22:57:40Z) + NextAuth.js v4.24.15 SHIPPED (npm `dist-tag.latest` moved 2026-07-20T23:19:38Z) + `@auth/core@0.41.3` SHIPPED (published 2026-07-20T15:00:00Z) on the same day, all carrying security advisory [GHSA-xmf8-cvqr-rfgj](https://github.com/advisories/GHSA-xmf8-cvqr-rfgj) (HIGH, CWE-20)** — the previous auth.md v1.4.99 entry still said *"NextAuth v5 beta has stagnated: beta.31 (April 14, 2026) is the latest, ~3 months old"*, which is now factually wrong (beta.32 ended the 3-month gap on Jul 20, with security fixes that should have triggered an immediate skill update). The headline v5-only fix: **auth checks no longer fail open on provider configuration errors** — a non-OK session response now returns `null` so `if (!!session)` style checks fail closed; previously a misconfigured provider returned an `Error`-shaped session object that truthy-checks passed. Pairs with malformed-Bearer `getToken()` fix (no more uncaught exceptions → request now returns 401 cleanly), provider-bound OAuth `state`/`nonce`/PKCE check cookies (closes a cross-provider confusion vector), and NFKC email normalization closing a homoglyph `@` bypass. Tenable Cloud Security tagged it as Plugin 445216 on 2026-07-23 (HIGH). v4.24.15 adds the same `@auth/core` patches plus v4-specific glue: explicit `NEXTAUTH_URL` precedence over auto-detected forwarded host (closes a redirect-host-injection vector behind trusted proxies), `uuid@^11.1.1` CommonJS pin (restores Node 18.x compatibility that the `uuid@14` ESM-only bump broke), and a one-time `OAuthSignInError` expected post-deploy from the state-cookie provider-binding change. **(2) `auth.md` had a Clerk coverage gap — `@clerk/nextjs` 7.5.12 (Jul 3, 2026) → 7.6.4 (Jul 31, 2026) SHIPPED 16 stable releases in 28 days, none of them documented in auth.md** (which only had a one-line table entry at line 12 and no dedicated `## Clerk` section at all). The two material ones: **`@clerk/nextjs@7.6.0` (Jul 23, 2026, PR #9223 by @thiskevinwang) — adds the `fapiUrl` option to Frontend API proxy helpers**, lets `clerkMiddleware()` route Clerk Frontend API requests at a custom Clerk Frontend API URL (EU/regional deployments behind a custom FAPI proxy, white-label deployments proxying through a corporate CDN, staging environments pointing at a non-production Clerk instance); and **`@clerk/nextjs@7.5.22` (Jul 21, 2026, PR #9207 by @mwickett) — removes the redundant `https://*.client.protect.clerk.com` source from CSP headers generated by `clerkMiddleware()`**, which fixes a long-standing CSP-bloat issue (the host was no longer needed) and breaks any deployment that relied on the source being present in a hand-written CSP. Added behind a new experimental flag `enableFlightWeakThenables`. Adds a new thenable status to the Flight protocol: `'pending_weak'`. Unlike a regular pending thenable, a weak thenable does **not** block the stream from closing. If it settles while the stream is still open, its value is emitted like a normal pending thenable. Otherwise its reference is left unfulfilled and on the client it stays forever pending, **without erroring**, even when the connection closes. It's up to the client to handle the unresolved promise in an appropriate way. **Motivating use case** — encoding metadata about a Flight stream into the response itself. For example, a framework might want to track whether a page varies by search params. It could represent this in the response as a `Promise<boolean>` that resolves to `true` as soon as the component being rendered in the stream accesses search params. If the thenable never resolves by the time the stream closes, then the client knows that no search params were ever accessed. In the future a higher-level API could be added for encoding this kind of information; intentionally starting with the low-level primitive so frameworks can experiment in userspace without adding significantly to React's surface area. Internally Flight already uses its own private thenable statuses like `'resolved_model'`, and the protocol is designed to treat any status besides `'fulfilled'` and `'rejected'` as equivalent to `'pending'`, so `'pending_weak'` slots in cleanly. **Practical impact: zero observable change today (flag off). The Flight Client side was harder to harden because `getOutlinedModel`'s path-walk also does object-identity cache deduplication, and skipping the wrong reference would break the outline cache — so the guard is precisely scoped to fire only when the value is **non-plain**. Common trust model (your own server, your own RSC, your own database) is invisible; the guard matters for cross-tenant RSC caching, cross-origin RSC widgets, and `dangerouslyAllowBrowser: true` consumers. **No API change, no config flag, no codemod** — pure hardening. Version bump 1.5.05 → 1.5.06. description: 
[30 Jul 2026 00:03Z] Routine 6h cycle — **React canary bump + canary-branch-ahead cycle (react@canary shipped 46 minutes after the v1.5.04 cron started, and Next.js canary.103 is staged but not yet published). Two weakest areas identified**: (1) **`react@canary` advanced `19.3.0-canary-96fcba90-20260728` → `19.3.0-canary-1724e9ce-20260729`** at 2026-07-29T18:48:34Z — 46 minutes AFTER the v1.5.04 cron's 18:03Z start time and BEFORE the next Next.js vendor-bump PR will pick it up. The previous cron completely missed this React canary (only 2 commits, but both materially important). The headline is **[React PR #37135](https://github.com/facebook/react/pull/37135) `[Fiber] Fix hang when updating a dehydrated boundary inside a hidden tree`** by dan — **closes Next.js issue #95848** ("Blank page when pressing Back between a reload and hydration with cacheComponents (regression in 16.3.0-canary.87)"), which was the entire reason **Next.js PR #95682** (`Replay same-document traversals that happen before hydration`) **got reverted in PR #95853** on 2026-07-15. The replacement PR **[#96252](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/pull/96252)** is open and explicitly waits for this React fix — so the **next Next.js canary after canary.103** (likely canary.104 or canary.105) will be able to un-revert #95682, restoring the "press Back during hydration, router replays the missed navigation" behavior. The second commit **[React PR #37125](https://github.com/facebook/react/pull/37125) `[DOM] Blur focused descendants in Fragment refs`** by Minh Vu is a smaller fix — `FragmentInstance.blur()` now matches nested focused elements (previously only the first level of host children), fixing a silent focus-leak in Fragment refs. No public API or config changes. (2) **Next.js canary-branch has 19 commits ahead of canary.103 (which is staged but not yet published — npm `dist-tag.next` still points to canary.102)** — and 8 of those commits are materially user-facing (most of the rest are docs, CI, and tests). The most material: **PR #96113 [fragment-scroll] Stop blurring on navigations** (Joseph, merged 2026-07-29T23:13:36Z — closes Next.js issue #96050, fixes the regression introduced in canary.71 where query-string-only `router.push/replace` blurs the focused input and dismisses the mobile keyboard; affects every form-heavy App Router app — search-as-you-type, filter inputs synced to URL); **PR #96364 Fix PPR rendering for configured HTML bots** (Zack Tanner, merged 2026-07-29T22:49:58Z — when `cacheComponents` was on, requests matching a custom `htmlLimitedBots` pattern bypassed PPR; the fix routes them through the existing streaming-metadata decision so the configured blocking-metadata behavior is now applied consistently — relevant for any project with custom SEO bot user-agent rules); **PR #96325 Share Ecmascript HMR chunk versioning, diffing, and merging between browser and node** (wbinnssmith, merged 2026-07-29T21:51:34Z — Turbopack: the `chunk_list/merged_update.rs` stack now lives in `turbopack-ecmascript/src/hmr/` (`version.rs`, `update.rs`, `content.rs`, `merger.rs`) and both browser and node runtimes share it via a `value_trait` on `EcmascriptHmrChunkContent` — eliminates the duplicated copy of the HMR machinery, fixes a copy-paste "chunk path ... is not in client root" error string that should have read "output root", and now applies node's lazy `entries()` materialization to the browser path so chunks with only deletions don't materialize any `Vc<Code>`; the unification of browser+node chunk-content structs is explicitly out of scope — needs `Box<dyn ChunkingContext>` widening because both chunking contexts define `minify_type` twice); **PR #96085 Ensure unique resolved `headers()` value between render passes** (Sebastian "Sebbie" Silbermann, merged 2026-07-29T22:16:35Z — a single HTTP request can render the same React tree in multiple passes with different semantics for `connection()` (the prospective and final prerenders of a runtime prefetch, or a navigation's dynamic render + the runtime prerender spawned from it to refresh the client's prefetch cache), and all of those passes previously resolved `headers()` to the same sealed headers object — so userland caches keyed on the identity of `await headers()` leaked promises across passes; the fix gives every render pass a distinct object over the same underlying data, making "the headers object identifies the request within one render pass" a real contract); **PR #96297 Gate partial fallback shell upgrades behind `partialPrefetching` for `next start`** (Andrew Clark, merged 2026-07-29T19:56:50Z — PR #96074 put `partialFallback` behind `partialPrefetching` for the deploy adapter but missed the `next start` path, which performs the upgrade itself in the compiled page runtime; this PR gates only the *upgrade* (the background ISR revalidation that specializes a shell per request + the client-facing `isFallbackUpgradeable` signal) — not the shell machinery as a whole — so build-time partial prerendering of params and serving build-time sub-shells continue working regardless of `partialPrefetching`); **PR #96180 Cache immutable current task IDs outside the task-state lock** (Marcos Hernanz, merged 2026-07-29T19:22:34Z — Turbopack `turbo-tasks`: introduces a cloneable `CurrentTaskStateHandle` that keeps the execution's immutable `Option<TaskId>` beside the existing shared `Arc<RwLock<CurrentTaskState>>`; `current_task_if_available` and `current_task` no longer take a shared `RwLock` on every native function call — the lock and its contention path remained visible in both HMR and production profiles; the absolute percentage is small (1–2% range, the PR's own evidence is directional) but it's also source-independent and applies to every execution); **PR #95646 Added cache copying support for worktrees** (Jimmy Miller, merged 2026-07-29T18:52:36Z — Turbopack now detects if it is in a worktree, finds the main repo, and copies turbopack caches for build or dev to make initial build faster; the implementation only looks at the root project (not other worktrees) — important for any monorepo where engineers use `git worktree add` to parallelize branches); **PR #96321 Bump @types/node to 20.17.7 to fix findSourceMap type** (dan, merged — fixes a type error that was silently failing in some Node.js 20.x types). [29 Jul 2026 18:03Z] Routine 6h cycle — **security.md + performance.md gap-fill cycle (Node.js July 27 security release was POSTPONED twice and PUBLISHED on Wednesday July 29, 2026 — 18 hours after the previous cron captured the pre-announcement but before it shipped). Two weakest areas identified**: (1) **`security.md` was 18 hours stale on the Node.js security release** — the v1.5.03 cron (Jul 29 00:03Z) only had the embargoed pre-announcement (HIGH ceiling + expected Node 22.24.x / 24.19.x / 26.4.x). The actual release went out Wed Jul 29 with **9 CVEs** (3 HIGH, 5 MEDIUM, 3 LOW) — patch versions **Node 22.23.2**, **Node 24.18.1**, **Node 26.5.1** — plus `undici` 8.9.0 / 7.29.0 / 6.28.0 + `llhttp` 9.4.3 dependency updates. The 3 HIGH CVEs: **CVE-2026-56846** HTTP/2 retained-headers maxSessionMemory bypass (remote memory-exhaustion DoS, 24.x + 22.x), **CVE-2026-56848** HTTP/2 re-entrant `nghttp2_session_mem_send` heap-use-after-free (26.x + 24.x + 22.x — the most operationally serious of the three, memory-safety class that frequently gets RCE’d), **CVE-2026-58043** Permission Model path-matching over-grant across radix-tree prefix boundaries (22.x + 24.x + 26.x — the first Permission Model HIGH of 2026, a security-boundary bypass not a DoS). The 5 MEDIUM: CVE-2026-56850 HTTPS Agent mTLS identity reuse across PFX certs, CVE-2026-58040 HTTPS Agent hostname-verification skip in TLS session reuse (incomplete fix for CVE-2026-48934), CVE-2026-58041 node:sqlite SQLTagStore iterator write replay, CVE-2026-58042 dns.resolveAny() abort on >256 A records, CVE-2026-58045 node:zlib sync spoofed-TypedArray crash. The 3 LOW: CVE-2026-56847 Permission Model trace_events filesystem bypass, CVE-2026-58039 Permission Model process.report filesystem bypass, CVE-2026-58044 HTTP parser header-truncation request smuggling. **The two-day postpone (Mon Jul 27 → Tue Jul 28 → Wed Jul 29) is unusual** — nodejs.org cites "additional testing and validation" then "infrastructure issues" — so future pre-announcement windows should leave a 3-day buffer. (2) **Turbopack star-import string-key tree-shaking (PR #96319)** — the only material canary-branch commit ahead of canary.102 (most others are docs + CI). Adds a 6-line gate in `turbopack-ecmascript/src/analyzer/imports.rs` that recognizes the `MemberProp::Computed(ComputedPropName { expr: box Expr::Lit(Lit::Str(_)), .. })` form (e.g. `ns["foo"]`) and narrows the usage to just the literal key, instead of expanding to `All` (which defeats tree-shaking). Small but real barrel-pruning improvement for projects using the dynamic-key string-literal pattern (icon libraries, jQuery-style plugin registries, lodash-style utilities indexed by name). **Tracked upstream versions unchanged from 1.5.03**: `next@latest` 16.2.12, `next@backport` 15.5.22, `next@canary` 16.3.0-canary.102, `next@preview` 16.3.0-preview.10, `react@latest` 19.2.8, `react@canary` 19.3.0-canary-96fcba90-20260728, `typescript@latest` 7.0.2, `typescript@next` 7.1.0-dev.20260728.1, `vite@latest` 8.1.5, `vitest@latest` 4.1.10, `vitest@beta` 5.0.0-beta.7, `@biomejs/biome` 2.5.6, `tailwindcss@latest` 4.3.3, `better-auth@latest` 1.6.25, `shadcn@latest` 4.16.0, `@playwright/test@latest` 1.62.0, `@tanstack/react-query@latest` 5.101.4, `zustand@latest` 5.0.14. **Changes**: security.md (the existing `## Node.js July 27, 2026 Security Release — Patch Day (HIGH in Each Line)` section is **completely rewritten** with the actual POST-release content — section header renamed to `## Node.js July 29, 2026 Security Release — 9 CVEs / 3 HIGH (Originally July 27, Delayed Twice)`, the pre-announcement-only "What's Confirmed (pre-release window)" table replaced with a full 10-row "Release Versions & Affected Lines" table, three new subsections added — 9-row "CVE List — 9 Total (3 HIGH, 5 MEDIUM, 3 LOW)" table with explicit per-CVE affected lines + reporter/fixer + impact, 2-row "Bundled-Dependency Updates" table (`undici` 8.9.0/7.29.0/6.28.0 + `llhttp` 9.4.3), 6-step "Post-Patch Verification Recipe" bash guide with `process.versions.undici` / `llhttp` / `nghttp2` / `openssl` printed-version checks + a Permission Model regression test for CVE-2026-58043; Turbopack now has native first-class support for `import.meta.env.DEV` / `.PROD` / `.MODE` / `.BASE_URL` / `.SSR` — Vite-compatible API for build-mode constants. Until this PR, Turbopack only supported `process.env.X`; `import.meta.env.X` was undefined, forcing Vite-migrated codebases to rewrite every `import.meta.env.X` to `process.env.X`. That rewrite is **no longer required**. The 5 built-ins are statically analyzed and replaced at build time (DCE-friendly), with `BASE_URL` derived from `basePath` + Vite-compat trailing slash, and `SSR` as a new Turbopack-specific constant (true server-side, false in client bundle). (2) **Turbopack server HMR refactor cluster (PR #94948 + #95661 + #95795 + #95546, all by wbinnssmith, SHIPPED in 16.3.0-canary.101 at 2026-07-28T21:13:44Z)** — a 4-PR refactor that replaces per-chunk server HMR turbo tasks with a single firehose subscription that diffs every HMR chunk together. **Multi-second saving on both cold and warm builds in large apps.** `clear()` is renamed to `reEvaluateAllModulesExpensive()` to label directly that this is a costly operation. `Performance.md` had zero coverage of any of these. **Tracked upstream versions updated**: `next@canary` 16.3.0-canary.99 → **16.3.0-canary.102** (npm `dist-tag.next` moved 3 times in this 6h window: canary.100 at 2026-07-28T21:04:54Z, canary.101 at 2026-07-28T21:13:44Z, canary.102 at 2026-07-28T23:55:12Z; ## Critical Rules (Never Forget)

- **`'use client'` boundary** — Only add when you need browser APIs, hooks, or interactivity. Keep everything else server-side.
- **Server Components can't use hooks** — No `useState`, `useEffect`, `useContext` in server components.
- **Colocate data fetching** — Fetch data in the component that needs it, not prop-drill from the top.
- **Zod for all schema validation** — Never trust raw form/API data without validation.
- **Tailwind = utility-first** — Don't fight it. Compose utilities, don't fight the cascade.
- **Server Actions = mutations** — Use them for form submits and data mutations; fetch for reads.
- **`<Image>` over `<img>`** — Always use Next's Image for automatic optimization and CLS prevention.
- **Abort in-flight requests** — Use `AbortController` to prevent race conditions on navigation.
- **Types in, types out** — Mirror backend response types exactly. No `any` from API calls.

only fires on soft-nav, hard-nav was always correct via the server resolver; root cause was the optimistic-URL-commit in the Instant Navigations reducer — the prediction was committed up front and the resolved RSC payload (after the redirect) was treated as confirmation of the prediction when the redirect target had the same shape as the prediction; fix invalidates the prediction on a redirect discovered during navigation and re-resolves the route before the address bar is shown; touches `ppr-navigations.ts` + `reducers/server-patch-reducer.ts` + `router-reducer-types.ts`; full details in routing.md); **(3) Turbopack `experimental.cssChunking: ‘graph’` config schema breaking change** ([#95088](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/pull/95088) by sokra / Tobias Koppers, merged June 29, 2026 at 15:53:24Z — `moduleFactorCost` option REMOVED, replaced by `weightDistribution`; new per-group cost formula `chunk_group_weight * (chunk_size + request_cost)` where `chunk_group_weight = group_total_size ^ (-weightDistribution)`; defaults retuned: `requestCost` `20000` → `100000` bytes, `weightDistribution` default `0.1`; ## Pro Tips

- Use `create-next-app --typescript --tailwind --eslint --app --src-dir --import-alias "@/*"` for a fully typed Next.js project
- Run `npx tsc --noEmit` to type-check without building
- Use `shadcn@latest add <component>` to add components — they live in your codebase, not node_modules
- Use `next.config.ts` for all Next.js configuration (not `.js`)
- Use `react-hook-form` + `zod` for all forms — never manage form state with useState
- Enable React Compiler in `next.config.ts` with `reactCompiler: true` — eliminates most `useMemo`/`useCallback` manually
- Use Biome (`npx biome check`) for linting — 10–100x faster than ESLint
- Run `npx biome migrate --write` after every Biome upgrade to migrate your config for breaking changes
- Use `use cache` for all server-side data fetching in Next.js 16 — it's the explicit opt-in caching model

Start with `setup.md` to initialize a project, then `components.md` for shadcn/ui patterns.

## Next.js 16 Migration Notes

Key breaking changes from Next.js 15 → 16:

| Change | Impact |
|---|---|
| **`use cache` directive** replaces `unstable_cache` | New explicit caching API — mark data functions with `use cache` + `cacheTag` |
| **Implicit caching removed** — everything is dynamic by default | Old `fetch` caching patterns deprecated; use `use cache` explicitly |
| **PPR (Partial Prerendering) stable** — `cacheComponents: true` | Static shell + streaming dynamic content; no longer experimental |
| **Router scroll optimization** enabled by default | Previously scroll was reset on navigation; now preserved by default |
| Flat config default in `@next/eslint-plugin-next` | ESLint config format change |
| Deprecated `.turbo` config object removed | Use `turbopack` key in `next.config.ts` instead |
| `publicRuntimeConfig` / `serverRuntimeConfig` removed | Use environment variables directly |
| **`next lint` removed** | Use Biome (`npx biome check`) or ESLint (`npx eslint .`) directly |
| **`middleware.ts` deprecated → `proxy.ts`** | `middleware` export renamed to `proxy`; must be `async`; `matcher` moved to `next.config.ts` or exported from `proxy.ts` |

**Upgrade:** `npx @next/codemod@canary upgrade latest` (Next.js 16.2+) — automated upgrade CLI that handles codemods, config migrations, and breaking changes in one command. **In canary.72+ (PR #95312, June 30, 2026) accepts `-y, --yes` for agents/CI** — auto-enabled when stdin is not a TTY so AI coding agents no longer hang on the recommended-codemods multiselect. Alternatively `npx next upgrade` (interactive, Next.js 16.1+) or `npm install next@latest`.

## 1.4.77 — 2026-07-21T18:03Z

**JULY 2026 SECURITY RELEASE — ALL 9 CVEs NOW DOCUMENTED.** The July 21, 2026 security release shipped at ~16:00 UTC (16.2.11 / 15.5.21). Full CVE table added to `security.md`: 4 High (DoS via Server Actions, Turbopack middleware bypass with single i18n locale, SSRF via rewrites, SSRF via Server Actions on custom servers) + 5 Medium (Image Optimization SVG DoS, unbounded Edge payload, Server Function endpoint disclosure, cache confusion ×2). The live status checkpoints (T-24h through T+6h) removed and replaced with final resolution. `api.md` gained "Server Action Security Hardening (canary.92)" section covering 7 PRs: bodySizeLimit Edge enforcement, correct origin for custom-server redirects, exotic rewrite param encoding, server reference ID validation (closes CVE-2026-64643), basePath preservation in redirects, and two fetch cache key fixes (effective-request keying + byte-exact binary body hashing). `deployment.md` gained "July 2026 Security Releases" section documenting 16.2.11 (Active LTS) + 15.5.21 (Maintenance LTS) + canary.92 upgrade path, post-upgrade checklist, and the monthly cadence reminder (next: August 20, 2026). canary.92 non-security items: Turbopack middleware i18n single-locale fix, MPA form validation perf, SVG detectContentType perf, instant validation navigation fix, `use cache` error handling, docs AI agents guide expansion. React 19.2.8 (2026-07-21) — performance improvements when decoding RSC (PR #37087, eps1lon). TanStack Query 5.101.4 (2026-07-21) — patch on query-core 5.101.4.

## Critical Rules (Never Forget)

- **`'use client'` boundary** — Only add when you need browser APIs, hooks, or interactivity. Keep everything else server-side.
- **Server Components can't use hooks** — No `useState`, `useEffect`, `useContext` in server components.
- **Colocate data fetching** — Fetch data in the component that needs it, not prop-drill from the top.
- **Zod for all schema validation** — Never trust raw form/API data without validation.
- **Tailwind = utility-first** — Don't fight it. Compose utilities, don't fight the cascade.
- **Server Actions = mutations** — Use them for form submits and data mutations; fetch for reads.
- **`<Image>` over `<img>`** — Always use Next's Image for automatic optimization and CLS prevention.
- **Abort in-flight requests** — Use `AbortController` to prevent race conditions on navigation.
- **Types in, types out** — Mirror backend response types exactly. No `any` from API calls.

The 17 commits since canary.70 split into **eight material user-facing changes** (six Next.js canary-branch PRs + one Turbopack PR + one React canary PR that became the new canary-`92f4fda3-20260629`): **(1) fix: preserve repeated search params in client page segment cache keys** ([#94863](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/pulls/94863) by icyJoseph, merged June 29, 2026 at 11:54:29Z — silent stale-UI bug where `Object.fromEntries(new URLSearchParams(search))` collapsed `?foo=bar&foo=baz` to `{foo: ‘baz’}` in the client page segment cache key, causing cache collisions between `?color=red&color=blue` and `?color=blue`; affected `<Link>`, `router.replace`, `<form>` (next/form) soft-nav with repeated keys; fixed in `ppr-navigations.ts` + `segment-cache/scheduler.ts` + `route-params.ts` by switching to the existing `urlSearchParamsToParsedUrlQuery` helper which preserves repeated params as arrays; fixes issues [#92787](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/issues/92787) (filed against next 16.2.1-canary.38, April 14), [#93104](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/issues/93104) (filed against stable, April 21), and [#94821](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/issues/94821) (filed against canary.51, June 15 — next/form submission case); new e2e test at `test/e2e/app-dir/multi-value-search-params-stale/`; no API change, no config change, no opt-in flag; single-value URLs unaffected; **upgrade to canary.71+ or 16.3.0 stable to get the fix**; full details in routing.md); **(2) fix: client nav URL bar stuck on original URL after middleware redirect + rewrite-to-dynamic-route** ([#95207](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/pulls/95207) by acdlite / Andrew Clark, merged June 29, 2026 at 17:00:28Z — silent stale-URL bug where a click on `<Link href="/a">` with a proxy/middleware redirect `/a → /` AND rewrite `/ → /a` (where `/a` is a dynamic route reading `await params`) rendered the correct page content but left `window.location.href` stuck on `/a` instead of `/`; only fires on soft-nav, hard-nav was always correct via the server resolver; root cause was the optimistic-URL-commit in the Instant Navigations reducer — the prediction was committed up front and the resolved RSC payload (after the redirect) was treated as confirmation of the prediction when the redirect target had the same shape as the prediction; fix invalidates the prediction on a redirect discovered during navigation and re-resolves the route before the address bar is shown; touches `ppr-navigations.ts` + `reducers/server-patch-reducer.ts` + `router-reducer-types.ts`; new e2e test at `test/e2e/app-dir/redirect-rewrite-dynamic/`; **fixes [issue #95195](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/issues/95195) by amannn against 16.3.0-preview.5** with a [public Playwright reproduction repo](https://github.com/amannn/nextjs-16-3-bug-repro-redirect); full details in routing.md); **(3) Turbopack `experimental.cssChunking: ‘graph’` config schema breaking change** ([#95088](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/pull/95088) by sokra / Tobias Koppers, merged June 29, 2026 at 15:53:24Z — `moduleFactorCost` option REMOVED, replaced by `weightDistribution`; new per-group cost formula `chunk_group_weight * (chunk_size + request_cost)` where `chunk_group_weight = group_total_size ^ (-weightDistribution)`; defaults retuned: `requestCost` `20000` → `100000` bytes, `weightDistribution` default `0.1`; old `{ type: ‘graph’, requestCost, moduleFactorCost }` config throws a schema error in canary.71+ — string form `‘graph’` is unchanged and uses the new defaults automatically; full details in performance.md). **Plus [React canary `19.3.0-canary-92f4fda3-20260629`](https://www.npmjs.com/package/react) (cut 2026-06-29T17:11:25Z, replaces canary `68631c04-20260626`)** — 3 commits ahead of the previous canary, one of which is material. *(As of 2026-06-30T16:54:01Z, the React canary SHA has moved forward to `19.3.0-canary-e2731312-20260630` (replaces `92f4fda3-20260629`). The new canary is non-material for the skill — its 6 commits are devtools-facade work and a chrome-devtools-mcp integration; no new APIs or fixes relevant to documented patterns.)* **[React PR #36851](https://github.com/facebook/react/pull/36851) `[Float] Forward nonce option in ReactDOM.preloadModule()`** by udit / Udit Dewan, merged June 29, 2026 at 11:33:22Z — silent CSP violation where `ReactDOM.preloadModule(href, { nonce, as, ... })` accepted `nonce` in its public type but the implementation only forwarded `as`, `crossOrigin`, and `integrity` to the host dispatcher, dropping `nonce`; under strict `script-src ‘nonce-...’` CSP, the emitted `<link rel="modulepreload">` had no nonce and was blocked by the browser; `ReactDOM.preload()` and `ReactDOM.preinitModule()` already forwarded `nonce` correctly; 5 files, +37/-5 across `ReactDOMFloat.js`, `ReactDOMTypes.js`, `ReactFlightClientConfigDOM.js`, and the test suite; full details in security.md). The other 6 canary-branch commits since canary.70 are non-material (skill docs, CI, React upgrade bump, type improvement, internal Turbopack): `cc-adoption` skill tighten by Aurora Scharff ([#95225](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/pull/95225), docs-only), `unstable_rethrow` client-bundling fix by eps1lon ([#95196](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/pull/95196), internal bundling optimization, Closes #95189), Turbopack `server-reference-manifest` dedup by Tariqul ([#95242](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/pull/95242), internal bug fix), CC test command display fix by eps1lon ([#95267](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/pull/95267), CI), React canary bump in Next.js by Vercel Release Bot ([#95211](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/pull/95211), package.json only), `decodeReply` typing by mischnic ([#95263](https://github.com/vercel/next.js/pull/95263), type narrowing), `[changelog] Add 19.0.x, 19.1.x, 19.2.x patch releases` by eps1lon ([#36898](https://github.com/facebook/react/pull/36898), changelog only), `[test] coverage for multi-byte code units in stream APIs` by eps1lon ([#36900](https://github.com/facebook/react/pull/36900), test only); - **@playwright/test 1.61.1** (E2E — **1.61.0 (June 15, 2026)** shipped WebAuthn passkeys virtual authenticator via `browserContext.credentials.create/install`, `page.localStorage` / `page.sessionStorage` (origin-aware, replaces `page.evaluate('localStorage…')` boilerplate), `apiResponse.securityDetails()` / `serverAddr()` network parity with browser responses, `testOptions.video` modes parity with trace (`'on-all-retries'`, `'retain-on-first-failure'`, `'retain-on-failure-and-retries'`), `expect.soft.poll(...)`, `fullConfig.argv`, `fullConfig.failOnFlakyTests`, `testInfo.errors` AggregateError sub-entries, `-G` shorthand for `--grep-invert`, HAR + trace now include WebSocket frames, Ubuntu 26.04 host support, browsers Chromium 149.0.7827.55 / Firefox 151.0 / WebKit 26.5; **1.61.1 (June 23, 2026)** fixed five 1.61 regressions — `expect.extend` matcher-name shadowing built-ins, UI-mode API request byte count mismatch, trace-viewer WebSocket timestamps scaled by 1/1000, sync ESM loader crash on Node 22.15, pnpm workspace symlink `.ts` subpath resolution)

## Pro Tips

- Use `create-next-app --typescript --tailwind --eslint --app --src-dir --import-alias "@/*"` for a fully typed Next.js project
- Run `npx tsc --noEmit` to type-check without building
- Use `shadcn@latest add <component>` to add components — they live in your codebase, not node_modules
- Use `next.config.ts` for all Next.js configuration (not `.js`)
- Use `react-hook-form` + `zod` for all forms — never manage form state with useState
- Enable React Compiler in `next.config.ts` with `reactCompiler: true` — eliminates most `useMemo`/`useCallback` manually
- Use Biome (`npx biome check`) for linting — 10–100x faster than ESLint
- Run `npx biome migrate --write` after every Biome upgrade to migrate your config for breaking changes
- Use `use cache` for all server-side data fetching in Next.js 16 — it's the explicit opt-in caching model

Start with `setup.md` to initialize a project, then `components.md` for shadcn/ui patterns.

## Next.js 16 Migration Notes

Key breaking changes from Next.js 15 → 16:

| Change | Impact |
|---|---|
| **`use cache` directive** replaces `unstable_cache` | New explicit caching API — mark data functions with `use cache` + `cacheTag` |
| **Implicit caching removed** — everything is dynamic by default | Old `fetch` caching patterns deprecated; use `use cache` explicitly |
| **PPR (Partial Prerendering) stable** — `cacheComponents: true` | Static shell + streaming dynamic content; no longer experimental |
| **Router scroll optimization** enabled by default | Previously scroll was reset on navigation; now preserved by default |
| Flat config default in `@next/eslint-plugin-next` | ESLint config format change |
| Deprecated `.turbo` config object removed | Use `turbopack` key in `next.config.ts` instead |
| `publicRuntimeConfig` / `serverRuntimeConfig` removed | Use environment variables directly |
| **`next lint` removed** | Use Biome (`npx biome check`) or ESLint (`npx eslint .`) directly |
| **`middleware.ts` deprecated → `proxy.ts`** | `middleware` export renamed to `proxy`; must be `async`; `matcher` moved to `next.config.ts` or exported from `proxy.ts` |

**Upgrade:** `npx @next/codemod@canary upgrade latest` (Next.js 16.2+) — automated upgrade CLI that handles codemods, config migrations, and breaking changes in one command. **In canary.72+ (PR #95312, June 30, 2026) accepts `-y, --yes` for agents/CI** — auto-enabled when stdin is not a TTY so AI coding agents no longer hang on the recommended-codemods multiselect. Alternatively `npx next upgrade` (interactive, Next.js 16.1+) or `npm install next@latest`.

## 1.4.77 — 2026-07-21T18:03Z

**JULY 2026 SECURITY RELEASE — ALL 9 CVEs NOW DOCUMENTED.** The July 21, 2026 security release shipped at ~16:00 UTC (16.2.11 / 15.5.21). Full CVE table added to `security.md`: 4 High (DoS via Server Actions, Turbopack middleware bypass with single i18n locale, SSRF via rewrites, SSRF via Server Actions on custom servers) + 5 Medium (Image Optimization SVG DoS, unbounded Edge payload, Server Function endpoint disclosure, cache confusion ×2). The live status checkpoints (T-24h through T+6h) removed and replaced with final resolution. `api.md` gained "Server Action Security Hardening (canary.92)" section covering 7 PRs: bodySizeLimit Edge enforcement, correct origin for custom-server redirects, exotic rewrite param encoding, server reference ID validation (closes CVE-2026-64643), basePath preservation in redirects, and two fetch cache key fixes (effective-request keying + byte-exact binary body hashing). `deployment.md` gained "July 2026 Security Releases" section documenting 16.2.11 (Active LTS) + 15.5.21 (Maintenance LTS) + canary.92 upgrade path, post-upgrade checklist, and the monthly cadence reminder (next: August 20, 2026). canary.92 non-security items: Turbopack middleware i18n single-locale fix, MPA form validation perf, SVG detectContentType perf, instant validation navigation fix, `use cache` error handling, docs AI agents guide expansion. React 19.2.8 (2026-07-21) — performance improvements when decoding RSC (PR #37087, eps1lon). TanStack Query 5.101.4 (2026-07-21) — patch on query-core 5.101.4.
